title: Aomori — 青森
goal: Connect a familiar place name to trees, food, and a small shopping conversation.

cards.title: A New Prefecture, a Familiar Name

blocks.text: 青森
あおもり — Aomori

At the end of Hokkaido, you read “Next is Aomori.” Now the place on that final reading card becomes our next destination. Aomori is both the name of a prefecture and the name of its capital city. In this lesson, 青森 means the city unless we say “Aomori Prefecture.”

Aomori City's Nebuta Festival uses large illuminated floats. Apples are also an important part of Aomori Prefecture's food identity. We will borrow the apple-shop setting for language practice, without needing festival dates or complicated food kanji.
You already know how a lesson works. Today we use that foundation rather than starting the explanation of kanji again.

items: **Kanji:** 青 · **Useful meaning/reading:** blue; あお, 青い = あおい; common on reading セイ · **Radical and visible parts:** Radical 青, あお. Modern upper shape 龶 and lower 月-shaped section · **What the parts tell us:** These are recognition shapes. The lower shape is **not a reason to interpret 青 as “moon.”** Historical formation is more complicated.

**Kanji:** 森 · **Useful meaning/reading:** forest; もり; on シン · **Radical and visible parts:** Radical 木, き. Three 木 components · **What the parts tell us:** Repeated trees give a direct connection to a wooded place.

blocks.text: **青 + 森 → 青森 / あおもり.** Learn the complete place name. Breaking its spelling into “blue/green” and “forest” is a character reading exercise, not an account of how the city got its name.
Our first useful graph connection is **木 → 林 → 森**. The component you met in 札 and 樽 can now help you recognise an entire family of tree characters.

cards.title: One Tree, Two Trees, Three Trees

items: **Character/word:** 木 · **Reading:** き · **Meaning:** tree; wood
**Character/word:** 林 · **Reading:** はやし · **Meaning:** grove; woods
**Character/word:** 森 · **Reading:** もり · **Meaning:** forest
**Character/word:** 森林 · **Reading:** しんりん · **Meaning:** forest; woodland

blocks.text: 林 contains two 木 shapes; 森 contains three. This is a helpful pattern, not a numerical rule for how many actual trees make a forest.

**森に木があります。**
もりに きが あります。
There are trees in the forest.
Breakdown: 森に = in the forest; 木が = trees, the subject; あります = exist. Japanese does not need a plural ending on 木 here. We are reusing the existence pattern from Hokkaido.

cards.title: 青い Is a Whole Word

blocks.text: **青い** — あおい — blue.
青 is the kanji; the final い belongs to the adjective. This is the same kind of kanji-plus-ending pattern you saw in 小さい and 美しい.

**これは青いりんごです。**
これは あおい りんごです。
This is a green apple.

Why does “blue” appear in a sentence translated “green apple”? 青 also appears in established Japanese expressions referring to things English calls green. Learn **青いりんご** as an expression; do not conclude that 青い can replace every ordinary Japanese word for green.
りんご means apple. We use its kana spelling. You do not need to learn the difficult spelling 林檎 because 林 has appeared today.

cards.title: 食: From a Character to an Action

blocks.text:
**食べる** — たべる — to eat.
**食べます** — たべます — eat / will eat.
食 is also the food/eating radical, しょく. You met this component inside 館 in Hakodate. Here it becomes a formally studied character in a common verb.

The modern 食 shape has several smaller strokes, including a top 人-like shape. Recognise the whole food component first; adding the ordinary meanings of its visible pieces will not reliably explain the character.

**りんごを食べます。**
りんごを たべます。
I eat / will eat an apple.
を identifies what is eaten. The verb's ending changes, while 食 remains recognisable: 食べません = do not eat; 食べました = ate; 食べませんでした = did not eat. Reuse the four polite endings from Noboribetsu.

cards.title: 店: A Place to Buy Something

blocks.text: **店 / お店** — みせ / おみせ — shop.

店 contains **广**, まだれ, as its radical, and **占** beneath it. The shelter/building shape gives a useful place-related clue; 占 is associated with the historical sound structure. Do not read the word みせ by adding the readings of the parts.

**店でりんごを食べます。**
みせで りんごを たべます。
I eat an apple at the shop.
Compare **店に行きます** (go to the shop) with **店で食べます** (eat at the shop). This revisits Hokkaido's に-versus-で distinction in a new situation.
お in お店 is a common polite prefix. 店 is still the same word. You can understand either form without treating the prefix as a new kanji.

**買う** — かう — to buy.
**買います** — かいます — buy / will buy.

The indexing radical of 買 is **貝**, かい, shell. Its upper **罒** is a net-shaped component. Shells have a historical connection with value and exchange, making 貝 a useful money-related clue in many characters. That clue does not tell us the reading かう.

**りんごを買います。**
りんごを かいます。
I buy / will buy an apple.

**りんごを買いません。**
りんごを かいません。
I do not buy / will not buy an apple.
The object marker remains を. 買う and 食べる are different verb types, so learn their polite forms as words. We are not introducing a rule that every dictionary ending can be replaced with ます directly.

cards.title: この / その / あの Need a Noun

blocks.text: You know **これ / それ / あれ**, which can stand alone. These new forms point to a noun:

items: **Standalone:** これ — this · **Before a noun:** この + noun · **Example:** このりんご — this apple
**Standalone:** それ — that near the listener · **Before a noun:** その + noun · **Example:** そのりんご — that apple
**Standalone:** あれ — that over there · **Before a noun:** あの + noun · **Example:** あの店 — that shop over there

blocks.text:
**このりんごは百円です。**
この りんごは ひゃくえんです。
This apple is 100 yen.
Compare **これは百円です** (this is 100 yen) with **このりんごは百円です** (this apple is 100 yen). Do not say “これりんご.” The noun after この completes the expression.
**りんごと水** — りんごと みず — apples and water.

**この店でりんごと水を買います。**
この みせで りんごと みずを かいます。
I buy apples and water at this shop.
Breakdown: この店で = at this shop; りんごと水を = apples and water, the things bought; 買います = buy. The single を applies to the joined list.

Today と joins named items. It does not mean that any two whole sentences can be connected simply by placing と between them. Later in Hanamaki, we will reuse と with a different role: doing something **with** a friend.

**Learner:** すみません。このりんごはいくらですか。
すみません。この りんごは いくらですか。
Excuse me. How much is this apple?

**Shopkeeper:** 百円です。
ひゃくえんです。
It is 100 yen.

**Learner:** ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございます。
Thank you.
すみません can get someone's attention politely. ありがとうございます expresses thanks. In this practice scene, the price is fictional; it is not the current price of an Aomori apple.
Notice how much you already knew: いくら, 円, 百, です, か, and the idea of a shop setting. We have made a more useful sentence by adding a small amount of new language.

items: Choose “this apple”: A. これりんご / B. このりんご / C. りんごこの.
Complete “I buy water”: 水＿＿買います。 A. を / B. に / C. の.
Does 森 tell you that every word containing 木 is read もり?

blocks.text: **Answers:** 1 B: この needs the noun りんご. 2 A: water is the object of buying. 3 No: a shared component may give a meaning clue, but the word's reading must still be learned.
Now say or silently build: **この店でりんごを買います。** — I buy an apple at this shop. If you need help, identify the shop, the item, and the action separately before reading the full sentence again.

items: **Location:** 青森 — あおもり. City and prefecture share a name.
**Tree family:** 木 → 林 → 森; 森林 = しんりん.
**Colour:** 青い = あおい; “green apple” is 青いりんご, an established expression.
**Words/actions:** 食べる → 食べます; 買う → 買います; 店 = みせ.
**Grammar:** この/その/あの + noun; noun と noun; object を; action location で.
**Useful phrase:** すみません。このりんごはいくらですか。
**Components:** 木 helps with 林/森; 食 connects back to 館; 買 uses 貝; 青's modern lower 月-shaped section is not a moon explanation.
**Review:** 百円; これは…です; the polite negative/past endings.

blocks.text: **Lesson complete. Next location: Hirosaki / 弘前.**
